name: Shammah
overview: Shammah was a male warrior known as the Harodite and is listed as the eighth member among "the thirty," the elite warriors who served King David. His tribal affiliation is not recorded in Scripture, and there are no additional notes about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Shammah means "waste," while an alternative form, Shammoth, means "desolation." Both names are proper names and are not indicated to have been given by God, reflecting possibly harsh or challenging circumstances associated with the individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Shammah beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as one of David's mighty men. There are no known relatives or connections detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shammah's significance lies in his inclusion among David's elite warriors, known as "the thirty," highlighting his valor and trusted position in David's military forces. Being identified as the Harodite and the eighth in this distinguished group underscores his recognized role in the defense and expansion of David's kingdom. His mention, although brief, contributes to the understanding of the strength and loyalty within David's ranks.
